newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after modest rebound.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after modest rebound.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer as a modest rebound reversed the sharp declines of the previous two sessions although LME stocks continue to rise.
Analyst Jim Steel of Refco said further upside correction was expected Friday.

"This is a little bit more than a dead cat bounce, and I am looking for it to move up to 105.00 to 108.00 cents (in September contract)," Steel said. Any advance above this would be sold into, he added.
Most-active September settled 1.85 cents higher at 104.35 cents a lb, traded 104.90 to 103.40 cents. Spot July rose the same to 106.90 cents.
Despite the expected, though modest, rebound from heavily oversold levels, September copper is still almost seven cents lower than a week ago.
LME stocks continue to rise, up 2,000 tonnes Thursday to 136,325 tonnes. The steady increases would cap the market during the current seasonal slowdown in the U.S. and Europe, dealers said.
The LME cash to three months backwardation was stable at $110/$120 a tonne.
